A Japanese anime key visual with a painterly finish: an anime-style character with an elegant adult anime face, large expressive eyes, a small nose and mouth, fine coloured linework and soft cel-to-painted shading with painted highlights in the hair and fabric. Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance.
Face proportions: a short midface and a soft, gently rounded jawline with a small soft chin; any crown or headpiece sits above her hairline. Her eyes keep the shape and size described below.

2. CHARACTER

Face — her own: an elegant, refined presence; porcelain-pale skin; heart-shaped face; medium-sized eyes — peach-blossom eyes with a soft, curved lower lid, outer eye corners slightly lifted; gracefully arched brows; slim, delicate nose with a refined bridge; soft, full lips; clear crystal-grey eyes with tiny blue flashes; sharp winged eyeliner.

Her element, carried in her design: lutetium: a hard, dense silvery-white metal, the last and smallest of the fifteen lanthanides and the hardest and densest of them; found in 1907 by a Paris chemist, also a painter and sculptor, who split the earth called ytterbia once more and named the hidden younger element for Lutetia, the old Latin name of Paris, while a rival in Austria called it cassiopeium; woven with silicon and oxygen into scintillator crystals it throws a tiny flash of blue light each time a gamma ray strikes, the eyes of PET scanners; its slow decay over some thirty-seven billion years dates meteorites and the oldest rocks.
Anatomy: one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint; natural hands with five fingers.

3. COSTUME — FANTASY

Silhouette: a fitted breastplate and pauldrons above a gown skirt flaring to the floor — an elegant lady-knight silhouette. Only the overall shape is fixed; design the details freely in the element's materials and palette. This silhouette overrides the overall shape of the costume above.
Colours: hard silver-white, scintillation blue flash, river slate grey, Parisian cream and soft black.
Exposure (bold): her regalia opens to show skin — bare shoulders and arms between pauldron and bracer, a deep open neckline under the gorget with natural cleavage, a high slit in the tabard or robe showing the thigh; armor pieces stay on and symmetrical. Nothing slipped off. Intimate areas covered; no corset; keep the costume above, material and palette.

4. SCENE

This card: beside a carved stone pillar raised by the boatmen's guild.
Pose: Standing turned three-quarters toward the camera, weight on one leg, one hand resting at her side or hip.
Light: natural daylight or the world's own magical glow.
Composition: vertical 2:3 full-body framing with modest headroom and clear space below the boots — the whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet stays inside the frame, occupying about four-fifths of the image height, with the same camera distance in every world; her hands stay inside the frame. Camera level with her face with natural portrait perspective; her head level, chin neither raised nor tucked — no upward perspective on her face, no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.

5. CONSTRAINTS
One figure only; no text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (Lu) and atomic number (71) — and those only as part of the scene: engraved, embroidered or glowing on her costume, a banner, a sign or a machine, never as a floating label, corner badge, periodic-table tile, caption or overlay on the picture; no logo or watermark.
Avoid: flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face, plastic 3D-render finish, corset, bustle, Victorian tailoring, modern material, machinery.
